alternative: Pass the payload as a constructor parameter so it exists before delegation - class FileStream(val buf: Buffer) : Stream(buf) - or build it in a companion/factory function; where only behaviour is shared, use interface delegation (Base by value) or composition. Kotlin evaluates superclass-constructor arguments before any instance property is initialised, and interfaces carry no state to move the based-member into.
idiom_name: none - super(arguments) is evaluated before instance properties exist; pass a constructor parameter
implementation_notes: Kotlin documents the order precisely: during construction of a derived instance the base class initialization is the first step, preceded only by evaluation of the arguments for the base class constructor, which means it happens before the derived class's own initialisation logic runs - so when the base constructor executes, the properties declared or overridden in the derived class have not yet been initialized. The superclass arguments can therefore only be constructor parameters or self-contained expressions, never the object's own data; and with single class inheritance (interfaces cannot hold instance state, abstract members are off limits during construction) there is no second supertype to carry the member either. What replaces the structure is a parameter: pass the payload into the primary or a secondary constructor and hand it straight to the base - optionally re-exposing it as a property - or use a companion/private factory; where only behaviour is needed, interface delegation ('by') is Kotlin's documented alternative to implementation inheritance.
pitfalls: Properties declared in the derived class are uninitialised while the base constructor runs, so an open property read from a base init block sees null or 0 even when the derived code looks correct - Kotlin's documentation warns against using open members in constructors, property initializers and init blocks for exactly this reason.

A secondary constructor must delegate before it can execute any statement, so the payload cannot be produced by the object's own logic: anything needing instance state must be restructured into a parameter or a factory.

Interface delegation is not inheritance of state: the delegate is a separate object, so a case that needs a base bound to the object's own storage (identity, not value) stays impossible and needs composition instead.
